what: Fixed a game-crashing bug in the ReShade-addon path found from ReShade.log: the log stopped dead right after AddonInit's diagnostic warnings with no shutdown/further output, meaning NBA 2K26 crashed inside CheckModulesInMemory(). Root cause: KernelBaseProxy::Init() (and NtdllProxy::Init()/Kernel32Proxy::Init()) are never called on the .addon64 path -- the DllMain guard added in Story 2 returns immediately after PrepareLogger(), skipping the proxy-DLL install's own Init() calls entirely. CheckModulesInMemory()'s first line calls GetDllNameWModule() -> KernelBaseProxy::GetModuleHandleW_()(), a null function pointer (StreamlineHooks::hookInterposer/hookDlss/etc. also depend on KernelBaseProxy::GetProcAddress_() the same way), causing a null-pointer-call access violation. Fixed by adding the same three Init() calls (same order, mirroring the existing _passThruMode branch) to the .addon64 guard in dllmain.cpp before it returns. Rebuilt Debug+Release x64 clean (0 errors, same warning baseline), refreshed OptiScaler.addon64.
why: Diagnosed from the user's live crash report + reading ReShade.log's abrupt stop, then traced the exact null-function-pointer call by reading GetDllNameWModule/KernelBaseProxy source rather than guessing

what: Verified live: the KernelBaseProxy::Init() fix stopped the crash -- ReShade.log for the retest shows a full 901-line session (device bridge, swapchain creation, shader compiles), no abrupt stop. Added an explicit reshade::log::message() report in AddonInit (OptiScalerAddon.cpp) of StreamlineHooks::isInterposerHooked/isDlssHooked/isDlssgHooked/isReflexHooked/isPclHooked/isCommonHooked immediately after CheckModulesInMemory(), so this lands in ReShade.log which we know gets written and read. Rebuilt Debug+Release x64 clean (0 errors), refreshed OptiScaler.addon64 and deployed it directly into the live NBA 2K26 folder.
why: Crash-fix verification needed direct evidence rather than assuming the hook attached just because the crash stopped; reusing reshade::log::message keeps verification independent of ini settings the user would otherwise need to change

what: Implemented the Streamline-RR-to-DlssNr redirect the user chose to build. Explicitly flagged in both the header comment and the plan file as unproven: built from reading Streamline's SDK headers and OptiScaler's own NGX-parameter contract, not from live tracing of what NBA 2K26's actual RR evaluate call carries. what: Pivoted from the ReShade-addon epic back to the original proxy-dxgi.dll install per the user's request, now that we have real log visibility (LogToFile forced on). Deployed a fresh OptiScaler.dll as dxgi.dll and got a full, successful OptiScaler.log: CheckWorkingMode succeeds, D3D12 device hooked, Streamline hooked, and critically NVSDK_NGX_D3D12_EvaluateFeature (OptiScaler's own substituted DLSS entry point) fires every frame with DLSSFeature::ProcessEvaluateParams showing correct render/target/display sizes -- DLSS override is genuinely working. The original 'OptiScaler doesn't work' premise from the very start of this session was a misdiagnosis: absence of OptiScaler.log was just LogToFile=auto (defaults false), not a load failure. However user reported the menu hotkey (Home, 0x24) doesn't work; traced this to a real, separate, narrower bug: only one CreateSwapChain-family call ever occurs in the whole session, flagged 'Overlay call!' (tiny dimensions, almost certainly Steam overlay's own auxiliary swapchain) -- the game's real swapchain is never captured (no 'Created new WrappedIDXGISwapChain' success log ever appears), so the menu (driven off the wrapped swapchain's Present) never initializes, while DLSS itself is unaffected since it doesn't need the swapchain. Found a likely root cause in DxgiFactoryHooks::HookToFactory (DxgiFactory_Hooks.cpp:70-73): a single global 'if (o_EnumAdapters != nullptr) return' guard assumes every IDXGIFactory instance the process ever sees shares one vtable/implementation, hooking only the first one it ever sees and silently skipping all subsequent factory objects -- plausible given the game's own log showed two near-simultaneous hkCreateDXGIFactory2 calls from NBA2K26.exe, and Steam overlay is almost certainly also wrapping/intercepting DXGI factory creation in this process. Added non-invasive diagnostic logging (does not change hooking behavior yet) capturing the raw factory pointer, Util::CheckForRealObject-unwrapped pointer, and vtable array pointer on every HookToFactory call, plus whether the guard would trigger and whether vtable slot 7 already matches the hooked original -- to get concrete evidence before committing to a fix, since a wrong fix here risks double-hooking or hooking a third-party overlay's proxy vtable instead of the real one. Rebuilt Debug+Release x64 clean (0 errors), deployed fresh dxgi.dll, cleared stale log.
why: User correctly pointed out the original NBA 2K26 investigation should be revisited now that LogToFile visibility is fixed, rather than continuing to build out the ReShade-addon epic for a problem (menu not working) that has nothing to do with the addon path at all

what: Diagnostic confirmed the vtable-sharing theory was wrong (all 6 factory objects in the session shared one vtable address) but also confirmed CreateSwapChainForHwnd is genuinely never called at all (zero occurrences of its own deep LOG_DEBUG line, not just the early-return warnings). Checked wrapped_factory.h's already-implemented CreateSwapChainForComposition to confirm IDXGIFactory2's real vtable ordering places it at index 24 (counted from IUnknown: 0-2 IUnknown, 3-6 IDXGIObject, 7-11 IDXGIFactory, 12-13 IDXGIFactory1, 14 IsWindowedStereoEnabled, 15 CreateSwapChainForHwnd, 16 CreateSwapChainForCoreWindow, 17 GetSharedResourceAdapterLuid, 18-23 Register/UnregisterStereoStatus*/OcclusionStatus*, 24 CreateSwapChainForComposition -- cross-checked against the existing code's own correct indices for 7/10/12/15/16/26, which line up with this same counting). DxgiFactoryHooks::HookToFactory (the default vtable-patching approach, active whenever DxgiFactoryWrapping=false) never hooked this slot at all -- only the object-wrapping approach (wrapped_factory.cpp, DxgiFactoryWrapping=true) implements it. A game creating its real swapchain via CreateSwapChainForComposition (DirectComposition-hosted presentation, plausible for a modern HDR-capable cross-platform title) would get zero interception: no crash, no log, matching the exact live symptom. Implemented the hook: added the vtable slot-24 DetourAttach to HookToFactory, and a new DxgiFactoryHooks::CreateSwapChainForComposition handler mirroring the existing CreateSwapChainForCoreWindow's plain-wrap logic (no FG/DX11 interop, since composition swapchains don't carry an HWND) almost line for line, substituting Util::GetProcessWindow() wherever the real hWnd would be used. Cleaned up the now-obsolete diagnostic logging from the previous investigation step (its vtable-slot-7-vs-o_EnumAdapters comparison was based on a wrong assumption about how Detours attaches -- it patches the target function's code in place, not the vtable slot's stored value -- so the comparison could never have been meaningful; left a short comment recording what was actually learned instead). Rebuilt Debug+Release x64 clean (0 errors), deployed, cleared stale log.
why: This is a real, well-evidenced, narrowly-scoped hypothesis (missing vtable hook, not a vague guess) built from ruling out the alternative theory first with live data rather than committing to a fix based on assumption

what: Live re-test showed the menu STILL doesn't initialize after adding the CreateSwapChainForComposition hook -- and critically, that hook never fired either (zero log lines from it, not even its own early-return checks). Combined with CreateSwapChainForHwnd also never firing (confirmed again) and DetourTransactionCommit succeeding (no 'Failed to hook IDXGIFactory' error), this rules out both prior theories (vtable-sharing gap, missing CreateSwapChainForComposition hook) -- DXGI only has 4 possible swapchain-creation entry points (CreateSwapChain, CreateSwapChainForHwnd, CreateSwapChainForCoreWindow, CreateSwapChainForComposition) and literally none of them ever execute a single logged line, despite the game visibly rendering and presenting frames to the user's screen. Investigated DLSSG_Dx12.cpp's separate HookToDLSSGFactory/DLSSGCreateSwapChain* path as a possible alternate route (Streamline's DLSSG plugin genuinely is loaded and hooked in this game per StreamlineHooks::hookDlssg firing) but confirmed it's a downstream consumer invoked FROM CreateSwapChainForHwnd/CreateSwapChain (via FGHooks::CreateSwapChainForHwnd), not an independent path -- dead end, since those top-level hooks never fire in the first place. New hypothesis, cheaper to test than the previous two: DXGI swapchain descriptors legitimately allow Width=0/Height=0 to mean 'use the window's client area' -- the existing 'if (Height < 100 || Width < 100) -> Overlay call!' classification would misfire on this legitimate pattern and skip wrapping the game's REAL swapchain, not just genuine tiny overlay swapchains (e.g. Steam's). The existing log never printed the actual dimensions of an 'Overlay call!' hit, so this couldn't be distinguished from the real Steam-overlay case. Added Width/Height to all 7 'Overlay call!' log sites across DxgiFactory_Hooks.cpp (both DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_DESC and DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_DESC1 variants, main and DLSSG-swapchain paths) -- a pure logging change, zero behavior change, to get a definitive answer before deciding whether to also handle the 0x0 case as a real swapchain rather than an overlay. Rebuilt Debug+Release x64 clean (0 errors), deployed, cleared stale log.
why: Two theories have now been ruled out on hard evidence rather than left unconfirmed; a third, cheaper-to-verify hypothesis (0x0 dimension misclassification) is worth testing with a pure logging change before writing any more speculative hook code

what: Confirmed via live OptiScaler.log that of DXGI's 4 swapchain-creation entry points, only classic IDXGIFactory::CreateSwapChain fires exactly once (Width=0,Height=0), and it gets classified as an 'Overlay call!' and passed through unwrapped; CreateSwapChainForHwnd/CoreWindow/Composition never fire at all (zero log lines from any of their branches, confirming they are never called, not silently filtered). Verified HookToFactory's hooking-once guard is legitimately safe (LOG_FUNC only prints on first factory, but hkCreateDXGIFactory2 confirms NBA2K26.exe's own later factory creation still routes through HookToFactory). Leading theory: the single 0x0 CreateSwapChain hit IS the game's real swapchain (created undersized then meant to be resized to window later, a legitimate D3D pattern), misclassified by the '<100 = overlay' heuristic since it never distinguishes a real 0x0 'size to window' descriptor from a genuine tiny overlay swapchain. Added Format/BufferCount/Hwnd/Windowed to that log line (pure diagnostic, no behavior change) to check whether OutputWindow matches the real game window before changing the classification logic.
why: Two prior entry-point theories were ruled out on hard evidence; rather than guess at a third hook to add, the only remaining swapchain-creation event actually observed needs full descriptor logging to confirm or refute whether it is the real swapchain before any behavior change is made

what: Confirmed the Width=0/Height=0 misclassification hypothesis: the sole real swapchain-creation call in NBA 2K26 (classic IDXGIFactory::CreateSwapChain) reported Format=28 (R8G8B8A8_UNORM), BufferCount=3, real Hwnd=0xAE1000, Windowed=1 -- a genuine game swapchain, not a helper overlay, just created with DXGI's documented 0x0 'size to window' idiom. Fixed DxgiFactoryHooks::CreateSwapChain: added a sizeToWindow check (Width==0 && Height==0 && OutputWindow!=nullptr) that now bypasses the '<100 = Overlay call!' skip-and-passthrough branch and proceeds through the normal wrap path instead; after o_CreateSwapChain succeeds with a still-0x0 localDesc, the real swapchain's GetDesc() is queried to read back DXGI's resolved buffer dimensions so State::currentSwapchainDesc/screenWidth/screenHeight don't end up bogus 0x0. Only the classic CreateSwapChain entry point was touched (the confirmed real path in this game); CreateSwapChainForCoreWindow/Composition were left alone since MSDN disallows 0x0 there and they were already confirmed never called in this game.
why: This is the first change in the whole swapchain investigation backed by a live-confirmed positive identification (real format/bufferCount/hwnd/windowed values) rather than a guess -- worth testing as the actual fix before considering any further hook additions

what: Hardened the Width=0/Height=0 size-to-window fix: user correctly flagged that trusting a non-null OutputWindow alone could misclassify a helper/overlay swapchain (Steam/Discord/NVIDIA overlay) using the same 0x0 idiom against its own hidden window as the game's real swapchain.
